buckets.name: Hard landing or tail strike
buckets.definition: A hard or bounced touchdown, or contact of the tail with the runway during rotation or flare.

include.text: The occurrence meets the CICTT ARC (Abnormal Runway Contact) definition.
Core definition: A hard or bounced touchdown, or contact of the tail with the runway during rotation or flare.

Matches 'Hard landing, tail strike' (SKYbrary – Hard Landing and Tail Strike): A touchdown with a vertical load above limits, a bounced landing, or contact of the tail with the runway during takeoff rotation or landing flare.
Narrative describes 'hard' (2 of 3 supporting reports).
include.quote: A late flare in gusty winds led to a hard landing and a tail strike.

include.text: Narrative describes 'led' (2 of 3 supporting reports).
include.quote: A late flare in gusty winds led to a hard landing and a tail strike.

include.text: Narrative describes 'strike' (2 of 3 supporting reports).
include.quote: A late flare in gusty winds led to a hard landing and a tail strike.

exclude.text: Coded RE (Runway Excursion) rather than ARC: similar wording, different occurrence category.
exclude.quote: Braking action was poor and the aircraft overran the runway end by 60 metres into the runway end safety area.

exclude.text: Coded RI (Runway Incursion) rather than ARC: similar wording, different occurrence category.
exclude.quote: After a late runway change the crew did not rebrief the approach and landed on Runway 35L instead of the assigned Runway 35R.

exclude.text: Not 'Anomaly: Ground Excursion – Runway' — that definition is crosswalked to RE, not ARC.
Not 'Wrong-surface event' — that definition is crosswalked to RI, not ARC.

examples.quote: A late flare in gusty winds led to a hard landing and a tail strike.
A bounced landing was followed by a hard second touchdown that damaged the nose landing gear.
An incorrect takeoff weight in the flight management computer led to early rotation and a tail strike on takeoff.

buckets.name: Takeoff after de-icing holdover time exceeded
buckets.definition: The aircraft is delayed after ground de-icing and the fluid holdover time is exceeded before takeoff.

include.text: The occurrence meets the CICTT ICE (Icing) definition.
Core definition: The aircraft is delayed after ground de-icing and the fluid holdover time is exceeded before takeoff.

Matches 'Holdover time' (FAA holdover time guidelines (ground de-icing and anti-icing)): The estimated time a de-icing or anti-icing fluid protects aircraft surfaces from frost or ice; if it is exceeded before takeoff, the aircraft must be checked or de-iced again.

exclude.text: Not 'Anomaly: Ground Incursion – Runway or Taxiway' — that definition is crosswalked to RI, not ICE.
Not 'Anomaly: Ground Excursion – Runway' — that definition is crosswalked to RE, not ICE.
Not 'Runway incursion' — that definition is crosswalked to RI, not ICE.
Events better described by CICTT RE (Runway Excursion) (runner-up parent, margin 0.73).

examples.quote: The takeoff was delayed beyond the de-icing fluid holdover time, and the crew returned to the pad for a second de-icing.

buckets.name: Upset or stall after unreliable airspeed
buckets.definition: Disagreeing or erroneous airspeed indications, for example from icing or pitot failure, lead to a stall warning, overspeed or upset in flight.

include.text: The occurrence meets the CICTT LOC-I (Loss of Control – Inflight) definition.
Core definition: Disagreeing or erroneous airspeed indications, for example from icing or pitot failure, lead to a stall warning, overspeed or upset in flight.

Matches 'Unreliable airspeed' (SKYbrary – Unreliable Airspeed): Erroneous or disagreeing airspeed indications, for example from pitot icing, ice crystals or a blocked pitot tube, which can lead to an upset if the crew follows the wrong indication.

Matches 'Loss of control in-flight' (IATA – Loss of Control In-flight (LOC-I)): A significant, unintended departure of the aircraft from controlled flight, such as a stall, spin or upset, often following a system malfunction or crew response to erroneous indications.
Narrative describes 'reached' (2 of 3 supporting reports).
include.quote: The autopilot disconnected and the aircraft reached a stall warning before the crew recovered.

include.text: Narrative describes 'recovered' (2 of 3 supporting reports).
include.quote: The autopilot disconnected and the aircraft reached a stall warning before the crew recovered.

exclude.text: Coded SCF-NP (System/Component Failure – Non-Powerplant) rather than LOC-I: similar wording, different occurrence category.
exclude.quote: The crew used the unreliable airspeed checklist, flew pitch and power, and returned to the departure airport without further problems.

exclude.text: Coded ICE (Icing) rather than LOC-I: similar wording, different occurrence category.
exclude.quote: The takeoff was delayed beyond the de-icing fluid holdover time, and the crew returned to the pad for a second de-icing.

exclude.text: Coded BIRD (Bird) rather than LOC-I: similar wording, different occurrence category.
exclude.quote: There was no indication in flight.

exclude.text: Events better described by CICTT ICE (Icing) (runner-up parent, margin 0.05).

examples.quote: The autopilot disconnected and the aircraft reached a stall warning before the crew recovered.
The stick shaker activated and the aircraft descended 3,000 feet during the upset before control was regained.
The crew pitched down in response, reached an overspeed and lost significant altitude before recovering.

parents.name: Airprox / ACAS alert / loss of separation / near midair / midair collision

buckets.name: TCAS resolution advisory after an altitude deviation
buckets.definition: The aircraft deviates from its cleared altitude (level bust) and traffic receives a TCAS resolution advisory or separation is lost.

include.text: The occurrence meets the CICTT MAC (Airprox / ACAS alert / loss of separation / near midair / midair collision) definition.
Core definition: The aircraft deviates from its cleared altitude (level bust) and traffic receives a TCAS resolution advisory or separation is lost.

Matches 'Level bust (altitude deviation)' (EUROCONTROL – Level bust): An unauthorised vertical deviation of more than 300 feet from the cleared flight level or altitude, a common cause of loss of separation and TCAS resolution advisories.

Matches 'Resolution advisory (RA)' (ICAO Annex 10 – Airborne Collision Avoidance System (ACAS)): An ACAS or TCAS indication to the flight crew recommending a vertical manoeuvre to increase separation from conflicting traffic.
Narrative describes 'advisory' (3 of 3 supporting reports).
include.quote: The resulting level bust triggered a TCAS climb resolution advisory and separation was lost.

include.text: Narrative describes 'resolution' (3 of 3 supporting reports).
include.quote: The resulting level bust triggered a TCAS climb resolution advisory and separation was lost.

include.text: Narrative describes 'altitude' (2 of 3 supporting reports).
include.quote: The climbing aircraft overshot its cleared altitude of FL240 by 400 feet, and opposite-direction traffic received a TCAS resolution advisory to descend.

exclude.text: Events better described by CICTT NAV (Navigation Error) (runner-up parent, margin 0.68).

examples.quote: The resulting level bust triggered a TCAS climb resolution advisory and separation was lost.
The climbing aircraft overshot its cleared altitude of FL240 by 400 feet, and opposite-direction traffic received a TCAS resolution advisory to descend.
Autopilot mode confusion caused an altitude deviation, and the crew received a TCAS resolution advisory for traffic 600 feet below.

buckets.name: Overrun after a long or fast landing on a wet or contaminated runway
buckets.definition: The aircraft touches down long or fast on a wet or contaminated runway, braking is poor, and it overruns the runway end.

include.text: The occurrence meets the CICTT RE (Runway Excursion) definition.
Core definition: The aircraft touches down long or fast on a wet or contaminated runway, braking is poor, and it overruns the runway end.
Matches 'Anomaly: Ground Excursion – Runway' (NASA ASRS coding taxonomy): An aircraft departs the runway surface during the takeoff or landing roll, including overruns after a long or fast landing.

Matches 'Runway condition code (RWYCC)' (ICAO Global Reporting Format (GRF) for runway surface conditions): A runway condition code from 6 (dry) down to 0 reports braking performance on wet or contaminated runways (water, slush, snow, ice), so crews can recompute landing distance.
Narrative describes 'runway' (3 of 3 supporting reports).
include.quote: Braking action was poor and the aircraft overran the runway end by 60 metres into the runway end safety area.

include.text: Narrative describes 'area' (2 of 3 supporting reports).
include.quote: Braking action was poor and the aircraft overran the runway end by 60 metres into the runway end safety area.

include.text: Narrative describes 'end' (2 of 3 supporting reports).

exclude.text: Not 'Anomaly: Ground Incursion – Runway or Taxiway' — that definition is crosswalked to RI, not RE.
Not 'Wrong-surface event' — that definition is crosswalked to RI, not RE.
Not 'Runway incursion' — that definition is crosswalked to RI, not RE.
Events better described by CICTT SCF-PP (System/Component Failure – Powerplant) (runner-up parent, margin 0.48).

examples.quote: Braking action was poor and the aircraft overran the runway end by 60 metres into the runway end safety area.
With one thrust reverser unavailable, a long landing on a contaminated runway ended in a low-speed overrun past the runway end.
After an unstabilized, fast approach the aircraft touched down 2,500 feet beyond the threshold on a runway reported with standing water and came to a stop in the overrun area.

buckets.name: Landing or takeoff on an unintended surface
buckets.definition: The aircraft lands, lines up to land, or starts a takeoff on a surface other than the assigned runway: a taxiway, a closed or wrong runway, or the wrong airport.

include.text: The occurrence meets the CICTT RI (Runway Incursion) definition.
Core definition: The aircraft lands, lines up to land, or starts a takeoff on a surface other than the assigned runway: a taxiway, a closed or wrong runway, or the wrong airport.

Matches 'Wrong-surface event' (FAA Runway Safety programme): A landing, attempted landing, line-up or takeoff on a surface other than the one assigned: a wrong runway, a taxiway, a closed runway or the wrong airport.

Matches 'Anomaly: Ground Incursion – Runway or Taxiway' (NASA ASRS coding taxonomy): An aircraft, vehicle or person entering a runway or taxiway without authorization, or an aircraft using a taxiway or the wrong runway for landing or takeoff.
Narrative describes 'approach' (2 of 5 supporting reports).
include.quote: During a night visual approach to Runway 27R the crew lined up on the parallel taxiway, mistaking the taxiway edge lights for runway lights.

include.text: Narrative describes 'instead' (2 of 5 supporting reports).

include.text: Narrative describes 'takeoff' (2 of 5 supporting reports).

buckets.name: Runway entry or crossing without clearance
buckets.definition: An aircraft or vehicle crosses a hold-short line, stop bar or holding point and enters an active runway without a clearance.

include.text: The occurrence meets the CICTT RI (Runway Incursion) definition.
Core definition: An aircraft or vehicle crosses a hold-short line, stop bar or holding point and enters an active runway without a clearance.

Matches 'Anomaly: Ground Incursion – Runway or Taxiway' (NASA ASRS coding taxonomy): An aircraft, vehicle or person entering a runway or taxiway without authorization, or an aircraft using a taxiway or the wrong runway for landing or takeoff.

Matches 'Runway incursion' (ICAO Doc 9870, Manual on the Prevention of Runway Incursions): Any occurrence at an aerodrome involving the incorrect presence of an aircraft, vehicle or person on the protected area of a surface designated for the landing and takeoff of aircraft.

Matches 'Runway incursion types' (FAA Runway Safety programme): Runway incursions are classified by cause as pilot deviations, operational incidents (controller actions) or vehicle and pedestrian deviations, and by severity from A to D.
Narrative describes 'clearance' (4 of 4 supporting reports).
include.quote: The stop bar lights were on, but the crew continued past the holding point onto the runway after mistaking a frequency change for a crossing clearance.

include.text: Narrative describes 'runway' (3 of 4 supporting reports).
include.quote: The stop bar lights were on, but the crew continued past the holding point onto the runway after mistaking a frequency change for a crossing clearance.

include.text: Narrative describes 'active' (2 of 4 supporting reports).

exclude.text: Distinguish from sibling C1 'Landing or takeoff on an unintended surface' under the same parent.
Not 'Anomaly: Ground Excursion – Runway' — that definition is crosswalked to RE, not RI.
Not 'Runway excursion (veer-off and overrun)' — that definition is crosswalked to RE, not RI.
Not 'Runway condition code (RWYCC)' — that definition is crosswalked to RE, not RI.
Events better described by CICTT RE (Runway Excursion) (runner-up parent, margin 0.75).

examples.quote: The stop bar lights were on, but the crew continued past the holding point onto the runway after mistaking a frequency change for a crossing clearance.
A readback error led the crew to hear cross Runway 9 instead of hold short of Runway 9, and the aircraft entered the active runway without a clearance.
Taxiing to Runway 16, the crew crossed the hold-short line for Runway 22 without a clearance while another aircraft was on its takeoff roll.
A snow removal vehicle entered the active runway without a clearance during clearing operations.

buckets.name: Engine damage or shutdown after bird ingestion
buckets.definition: Birds ingested into an engine cause vibration, surge, loss of thrust, fire warning or shutdown.

include.text: The occurrence meets the CICTT SCF-PP (System/Component Failure – Powerplant) definition.
Core definition: Birds ingested into an engine cause vibration, surge, loss of thrust, fire warning or shutdown.

Matches 'Engine bird ingestion' (14 CFR 33.76 – Bird ingestion (engine certification)): Engines must be shown to withstand the ingestion of birds of defined sizes; large or multiple bird ingestion can damage fan blades and cause surge, loss of thrust, shutdown or fire.
Narrative describes 'engine' (3 of 3 supporting reports).
include.quote: After ingesting a large bird at 3,000 feet the crew received an engine fire warning, shut the engine down and discharged the fire extinguisher.

include.text: Narrative describes 'bird' (2 of 3 supporting reports).

examples.quote: After ingesting a large bird at 3,000 feet the crew received an engine fire warning, shut the engine down and discharged the fire extinguisher.

buckets.name: Clear-air turbulence with cabin injuries
buckets.definition: An unexpected encounter with turbulence in clear air injures passengers or cabin crew who are standing, unbelted or near unsecured carts.

include.text: The occurrence meets the CICTT TURB (Turbulence Encounter) definition.
Core definition: An unexpected encounter with turbulence in clear air injures passengers or cabin crew who are standing, unbelted or near unsecured carts.

Matches 'Clear-air turbulence (CAT)' (SKYbrary – Clear Air Turbulence): Turbulence in cloud-free air, often near jet streams or over mountains, with no visual cue and often not shown on weather radar.

Matches 'Turbulence-related injuries' (FAA Advisory Circular 120-88A – Preventing Injuries Caused by Turbulence): Passengers and flight attendants are injured in turbulence mainly when standing or not wearing seat belts, and by unsecured carts and galley equipment.
Narrative describes 'attendant' (2 of 4 supporting reports).
include.quote: Moderate to severe clear-air turbulence over the mountains caught the cabin with carts not secured, and a flight attendant was struck by a cart.

include.text: Narrative describes 'injured' (2 of 4 supporting reports).
include.quote: Three passengers who were not wearing seat belts were injured.

include.text: Narrative describes 'passengers' (2 of 4 supporting reports).
include.quote: Three passengers who were not wearing seat belts were injured.

exclude.text: Events better described by CICTT CABIN (Cabin Safety Events) (runner-up parent, margin 0.02).

examples.quote: Moderate to severe clear-air turbulence over the mountains caught the cabin with carts not secured, and a flight attendant was struck by a cart.
